artifact_role: SNARK-origin proofcore recovery overlay; not canonical release

findings.finding: User-provided history says the project began as a SNARKs-adjacent proof exploration. The carried canonical indexes support a still-visible proof lineage across zkrtp, streamfold, sumcheck/FRI/PCS/Halo2 ABI IR, receipts, attestations, witnesses, and verifiers.
findings.recommended_change: Make a first-class proofcore lane instead of letting the proof work remain hidden inside publication/rights/governance infrastructure.

findings.finding: The carried canonical index exposes 1067 broad proof-signal paths, but 0 of those paths are present as payload files in this overlay ZIP. The overlay is therefore a map to the proof core, not the proof core itself.
findings.recommended_change: Recover or mount the full canonical tree before attempting mathematical/protocol validation. Until then, audit against hashes, file inventory, rights ledger, and patch evidence only.

findings.finding: The rights ledger records zkrtp as 193 files / 18,902,244 bytes and streamfold as 83 files / 2,778,263 bytes, both represented without retained source/root and both blocked pending license decisions.
findings.recommended_change: Treat zkrtp and streamfold as critical recovery components: restore source roots, map paper/spec/render/artifact/cert relationships, and resolve rights before publication or external proof claims.

findings.finding: The index suggests a rich proof-adjacent ecosystem, but the overlay does not expose an executable contract that binds claims to verifier code, circuit/constraint representations, public inputs, witness policy, parameters, and expected outputs.
findings.recommended_change: Add a canonical PROOFCORE/ lane with threat model, claim schema, commitment map, verifier harness, proof-system parameter registry, and minimal acceptance vectors.

findings.finding: The project hardened publication, symlink, overlay, and rights boundaries repeatedly. That work is useful, but the new origin context implies it may have displaced the older proof question instead of completing it.
findings.recommended_change: Put infrastructure work behind a proofcore threat-model gate: only add new hardening when it protects a named proofcore, publication, or rights invariant.

findings.finding: No root LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE, component license conclusions, or missing local rights target has been resolved. The proof-origin context does not reduce the publication rights block; it increases the need for source/root clarity.
findings.recommended_change: Do not publish or assert redistribution rights. Resolve human owner/upstream decisions, then regenerate RIGHTS, SPDX, RO-Crate, and proofcore provenance surfaces from the same source of truth.

missing_piece_register: Canonical PROOFCORE/ lane with threat model and glossary: SNARK, ZK, succinct argument, certificate, receipt, attestation, verifier, witness, public input.
Claim-to-proof map: every paper/spec claim should point to a machine-checkable schema, verifier, public input, witness policy, or explicit non-machine-checkable status.
Verifier harness and acceptance vectors for the proof-adjacent artifacts already named in the index.
Proof-system parameter registry: commitment scheme, curve/hash assumptions, setup/trusted-setup status, transcript/Fiat-Shamir domain separation, verifier key identity, and versioning.
Source/root recovery for zkrtp and streamfold, which the rights ledger currently records as represented without retained source/root.
Rights closure before public redistribution or external claims.
Patch-bundle identity separated from canonical proofcore identity and signed provenance for both.

mission_reframe.long: The vault should bind claims, evidence, source snapshots, public inputs, verifier code, proof/certificate artifacts, rights, and provenance so a future operator can distinguish mathematical/protocol validity from archival integrity, publication permission, and governance attestation.
mission_reframe.short: EvidenceVault should preserve a proof-carrying research object, not just a publication bundle.

non_actions: No root LICENSE, COPYING, NOTICE, component conclusion, SPDX rights assertion, or RO-Crate rights assertion was added.
No claim is made that the overlay contains runnable SNARK/verifier payloads; the proofcore evidence here is from carried canonical indexes and ledgers.
No mathematical correctness claim is made for any named protocol artifact.
recommended_changes_ordered: Create PROOFCORE_RECOVERY_PLAN_REV0852.md as the immediate operator map.
Recover/mount the full canonical tree before interpreting the proof payloads themselves.
Classify proof-signal paths into papers, executable verifiers, schemas, ABI IR, certificates/attestations, receipts, witnesses, renders, and non-proof governance.
Choose an explicit scope: actual zero-knowledge/SNARK proof system versus SNARK-adjacent proof-carrying receipt/certificate system.
Make a minimal green path: one claim, one public input, one verifier, one fixture, one expected accept/reject result, one rights decision.
Only then resume broader publication hardening or full-tree regeneration.

research_notes.note: zk-SNARK is commonly expanded as Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-Interactive Argument of Knowledge: a proof construction where a prover can show possession/validity without revealing the witness and without prover/verifier interaction.

Groth16 is a central pairing-based non-interactive argument construction; the project should avoid implying Groth16/PLONK/STARK/Halo2 use unless a recovered artifact actually binds to one of those systems.

Proof-carrying data attaches proofs to messages/outputs so components can check that the output data satisfies prescribed properties; this is a close conceptual fit for EvidenceVault if its receipts/claims become checkable proof-bearing objects.
in-toto attestations are authenticated metadata intended for policy engines; this matches the datacube tendency to bundle DSSE/statements with artifacts.
SLSA provenance records that a build platform produced artifacts by executing a build definition. This is useful infrastructure, but it is not a substitute for mathematical proof-system verification.

RO-Crate describes research objects by linking data, methods, outputs, outcomes, and context; EvidenceVault already resembles that shape, but needs the proofcore lane as a first-class research-object component.
SPDX NOASSERTION is not a license grant or conclusion. It correctly preserves uncertainty but cannot unblock publication.

source_context.interpretation: This reframes EvidenceVault as a proof-carrying evidence/research object whose archive machinery should serve a recoverable proofcore.
source_context.user_supplied_origin: Project began as a SNARKs-adjacent proof exploration and that was the core for most of its life.

speculative_read: The project may have migrated from cryptographic succinct proofs toward a broader proof-carrying governance/evidence system because verifiable publication, rights, and provenance became prerequisites for sharing the proof work. That migration is understandable, but the proof core needs to be surfaced again or the archive will optimize everything except its original research question.
